metaDescription: Own mineral or coalbed methane rights under Tarrant, AL? We evaluate Jefferson County parcels against Black Warrior Basin activity and make a written cash offer.
heroLead: Tarrant sits inside the old Jefferson County mineral district, where deeds were carved off steel-era land companies decades before anyone drilled a CBM well.
intro: Tarrant was platted as a company town for the steel mills that once anchored northeast Jefferson County, and much of its mineral estate still traces back to the land and improvement companies that assembled acreage there in the early 1900s. Those old severances mean a lot of Tarrant mineral owners hold an interest that has never generated a check, or one that produced modestly during the coalbed methane build-out of the 1990s and has been quiet since.

If your family holds a mineral certificate, an old royalty deed, or a fractional interest inherited from a Tarrant relative, we can tell you fairly quickly whether it sits near active Black Warrior Basin coal seam gas production or on acreage that a buyer would price mainly on optionality.

sections.heading: Where Tarrant sits in the coal seam gas picture
paragraphs: Tarrant itself is closer to the edge of the Black Warrior Basin's productive core than towns like Oak Grove or Brookwood further southwest, so wells directly under the city are less common than nearby degasification and CBM activity tied to the historic Jefferson County coal seams. That doesn't make the interest worthless. It changes how we price it: acreage near the fairway trades on recent offset well performance, while flank acreage like a lot of what sits under Tarrant trades more on a patient hold-and-wait basis, weighted toward what a future operator might do if gas prices or infrastructure change.

We pull the county's producing well index and any historic permits tied to your legal description before we quote a number, so the offer reflects where your specific tract sits, not a blanket Jefferson County rate.

sections.heading: Old company-town deeds and split estates
paragraphs: Because Tarrant grew up around Sloss and other steel and coal operations, a meaningful share of local mineral estates were split from the surface a hundred years ago, sometimes by companies that no longer exist under their original name. Tracing that chain through the Jefferson County Probate Court can take real time, and many owners come to us holding a deed that references a corporate grantor with an unfamiliar name.

We're comfortable running that chain ourselves. If your paperwork is a photocopy of a photocopy, or you're not entirely sure how many mineral acres you actually own, that's a normal starting point rather than a disqualifier.

sections.heading: What a Tarrant offer is built on
paragraphs: Our number reflects three things: your net mineral acres as they show in the chain of title, whether the tract is held by a current CBM unit or lease, and how nearby production has behaved over the past several years. Coalbed methane wells decline in a specific pattern, faster in the first few years and then flattening, so an offer on producing interest is tied to where the well sits on that curve, not a flat multiple.

For undeveloped or long-idle interest, we price against comparable Jefferson County transfers and recent royalty activity in the basin, always as a range that moves with what the market is actually doing rather than a promise of a fixed outcome.

faqs.question: I inherited a fraction of a mineral interest in Tarrant and don't know the acreage. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give us the legal description or even just the deed book and page from the Jefferson County Probate Court, and we'll work out the net acreage as part of our review before we quote anything.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling directly under Tarrant right now?
faqs.answer: Tarrant sits toward the edge of the historic Black Warrior CBM fairway rather than in its core, so we check current permits and producing wells against your specific parcel before we characterize activity level, rather than assuming based on the city name alone.

faqs.question: Do you buy small fractional interests as well as whole tracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, fractional and undivided interests are common in Jefferson County given how many of these estates split across heirs, and we price and buy those regularly.
